correctness.rationale: For every \(m\ge3\) and each positive weighted arm mass, the \(m+1\) nodal hats span a positive definite Gram matrix. Its exact block Schur complement is \(M/4\) and yields an explicitly checked inverse. The reproducing kernel at the center is \((4-6s)/M\), while the kernel on arm \(j\) at leaf \(i\) is \((-2+3s)/M+\mathbf1_{\{j=i\}}3s/\mu_i\). Exact absolute integrations give \(5/3\) at the center and \(7/3-4\mu_i/[3(M+\mu_i)]\) at leaf \(i\). Convexity along each arm reduces the operator norm to vertices; measurable kernel signs attain it. Monotonicity and \(\mu_*\le M/m\) give the unique optimal mass-balance condition and strict nonattaining upper envelope \(7/3\). A standalone exact rational script independently assembled, inverted and integrated 225 cases, but the universal proof is algebraic and does not depend on sampling.

value.rationale: The canonical one-affine-element-per-arm space is the lowest-order continuous spline approximation on a star-shaped metric network. The complete classification quantifies how a high-valence junction changes worst-case least-squares amplification, with a degree-independent sharp envelope \(7/3\), unique optimal allocation of weighted arm mass, a valence-dependent increasing minimum, and nonattainment phenomena. This is a motivated natural whole family, not an arbitrary fixed parameter or a minor numeric improvement; the \(m=2\) known case is excluded.
